2027-09-08.title: Nativity of Mary, Mother of God
readings: Whoever does the will of God is my mother
Where are you? The promise of the woman
You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you
The princess is decked in her chamber with gold
The virgin shall conceive and bear a son
A woman clothed with the sun
Standing near the cross of Jesus was his mother
2027-09-08.alt: Feast of the Nativity of Mary, Mother of God (Wednesday). The Eight Days' Fast ends.
2027-09-08.verse: A great portent appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
theo: Today the Church rejoices at a birth. According to ancient tradition, a daughter was born to Joachim and Anna, and they named her Mary. No angels sang over Bethlehem that day, but heaven rejoiced, for the one who would be the Mother of God had come into the world. The Church celebrates only three birthdays: the birth of Christ, of John the Baptist and of Mary, because each was holy from the very beginning.

In the garden God called: “Where are you?” Adam and Eve were hiding in shame. Then God promised the woman whose offspring would strike the serpent's head. Isaiah gave King Ahaz a sign: “the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel”; St Matthew reads it as fulfilled in the Virgin Mary (Matthew 1:23). With Mary's birth the dawn breaks before the Sun of Justice rises.

The Song of Songs sings: “You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.” The Church applies these words to Mary, who by a singular grace was preserved from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception. Her beauty is not her own achievement but the work of God's grace, preparing a worthy dwelling for his Son.

St John sees “a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.” She gives birth to the Son who will rule the nations, and the dragon is defeated. The woman is Mary and the Church together. Yet the Gospel reminds us what makes Mary great: “Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.” Her birthday invites us to be born again each day into doing God's will.
conn: The first promise.
Genesis 3:15: the woman and her offspring; Revelation 12: the woman and the dragon.
The sign of Immanuel.
Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23: the virgin and her son, God with us.
No flaw.
Song of Songs 4:7: “there is no flaw in you”; the Immaculate Conception.
Newness of life.
Romans 6:4: we walk in newness of life; Mary's birth is the dawn of the new creation.
altar: Mary was born to become the Mother of the One who is offered on our altars. In every Holy Qurbono the Church remembers her first among the saints and gives thanks for the flesh the Word took from her.
outline: A birthday in heaven and on earth.
Point 2 · The dawn before the sun
“Whoever does the will of God is my mother.”
live: Celebrate Mary's birthday
Honour Mary today with a Rosary or a visit to a Marian shrine.
Thank God for your mother
Remember your own birth and thank God for the mother who gave you life.
Protect life
Pray and act for the protection of unborn children.
fathers: Today the Creator of all has built himself a new temple; today creation is made ready for the indwelling of God. The birth of the Mother of God is the beginning of all the feasts (Sermon 1 on the Nativity of Mary).
O blessed couple Joachim and Anne! You have offered the world the Virgin, the Mother of God, through whom all creation is renewed (Homily on the Nativity of Mary 2).
magis: Catechism 490–493
Mary was enriched by God with gifts appropriate to her role; she was redeemed from the moment of her conception.
Catechism 489
Throughout the Old Covenant the mission of many holy women prepared for that of Mary.
Lumen Gentium 55
Mary is foreshadowed in the promise of victory over the serpent and in the virgin who will bear Immanuel.
saints: Sunday 12 September: VI Sunday after the Transfiguration. Tuesday 14 September: Exaltation of the Holy Cross (Sleebo).
2027-09-08.prayer: Lord God, you made the birth of the Virgin Mary the dawn of our salvation. Grant that we who celebrate her birthday may be born anew in your grace, do your will as she did, and come with her to the joy of your Son, who lives and reigns for ever. Amen.

2027-09-05.title: Fifth Sunday after the Transfiguration
readings: Pray always and do not lose heart
The Lord will not cast away his people
Commit your work to the Lord
I will never leave you or forsake you
What is impossible for mortals is possible for God
2027-09-05.alt: Season of the Transfiguration. St Teresa of Kolkata. The Eight Days' Fast ends with the Nativity of Mary on Wednesday 8 September.
2027-09-05.verse: He replied, “What is impossible for mortals is possible for God.”
theo: A ruler asks Jesus: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” He has kept the commandments since his youth. Jesus looks at him and says: “There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” The man becomes sad, “for he was very rich.” He was good, but something still held his heart.

Jesus says: “How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God! Indeed, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle.” The disciples are shocked: “Then who can be saved?” Jesus answers: “What is impossible for mortals is possible for God.” Salvation is never our achievement; it is God's gift. Only grace can loosen the grip of riches on the human heart.

Peter says: “Look, we have left our homes and followed you.” Jesus promises that no one who has left house or family for the kingdom will fail to receive very much more in this age, and eternal life in the age to come. Following Christ is not loss but gain. The Letter to the Hebrews says: keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, for he has said, “I will never leave you or forsake you” (Hebrews 13:5).

In the evening Gospel Jesus tells his disciples “to pray always and not to lose heart”, with the parable of the widow who keeps coming to the unjust judge. Moses, too, lay before the Lord forty days and nights, interceding for the people. Isaiah brings the answer of God: “Comfort, O comfort my people… He will feed his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms.” The God who makes the impossible possible also hears the persistent cry of his children.
conn: Moses intercedes.
Deuteronomy 9:26: “Lord GOD, do not destroy the people who are your very own possession”; intercession that does not give up.
Not cast away.
1 Samuel 12:22: “the LORD will not cast away his people, for his great name's sake.”
God directs the steps.
Proverbs 16:9: “The human mind plans the way, but the LORD directs the steps.”
The shepherd.
Isaiah 40:11: he gathers the lambs in his arms; Hebrews 13:5: he will never leave us.
altar: At the altar we offer bread and wine, small gifts, and God makes the impossible possible: they become the Body and Blood of Christ. He can likewise transform our hearts, freeing them from the love of money.
outline: A good man who went away sad.
Point 2 · The camel and the needle
Point 3 · Impossible for mortals, possible for God
Point 4 · Pray always, do not lose heart
The God who comforts and never forsakes.
“What is impossible for mortals is possible for God.”
live: Name your “one thing”
Ask in prayer what still holds your heart back from following Jesus fully.
Generosity
Give a real gift to the poor this week, not only from your surplus.
Pray without losing heart
Return to a prayer you had given up on, and keep praying.
fathers: The Lord does not command us to throw away our property, but to banish from the soul its attachment to wealth, which is a sickness of the soul (Who Is the Rich Man That Shall Be Saved? 11).
The bread you hold back belongs to the hungry; the coat in your closet belongs to the naked (Homily on Luke 12, 7).
magis: Catechism 2544–2547
Jesus enjoins his disciples to prefer him to everything and everyone; detachment from riches is necessary for entering the kingdom.
Catechism 2053
The rich young man: Jesus adds the call to follow him in poverty and chastity to the keeping of the commandments.
Catechism 2573
The persistent widow: prayer requires perseverance and faith.
saints: 5 September: St Teresa of Kolkata. 8 September (Wed): Nativity of Mary, Mother of God; end of the Eight Days' Fast. Sunday 12 September: VI Sunday after the Transfiguration.
2027-09-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, you looked with love on the rich young man and called him to follow you. Free our hearts from all that holds us back; make us generous to the poor; teach us to pray always without losing heart; and do in us what is impossible for us, by the power of your grace. Amen.

2027-09-14.title: Exaltation of the Holy Cross (Sleebo)
readings: The sign of the Son of Man in heaven
Jacob crosses his hands in blessing
David defeats Goliath in the name of the Lord
I was ready to be found by those who did not seek me
Through him forgiveness of sins is proclaimed
Christ redeemed us from the curse by becoming a curse for us
Stand up and raise your heads; your redemption is drawing near
2027-09-14.alt: Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross (Sleebo): the season of Sleebo, the last season of the liturgical year, begins.
2027-09-14.verse: Now when these things begin to take place, stand up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.
theo: Today the Church lifts up the Cross. According to tradition, St Helena found the Cross of the Lord in Jerusalem, and on 13 September 335 the basilica of the Holy Sepulchre was dedicated; the next day the Cross was shown to the people. The instrument of shame has become the sign of victory. We do not celebrate suffering for its own sake, but the love that went to the end and the life that came forth from death.

In the desert the people, bitten by serpents, looked at the bronze serpent Moses lifted up, and lived: “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.” Jesus said: “just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up” (John 3:14). Whoever looks to the crucified Christ with faith is healed of the poison of sin. St Paul says: “Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us; for it is written, ‘Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree’” (Galatians 3:13).

The Fathers saw the Cross foreshadowed everywhere. Jacob, blessing Joseph's sons, crossed his hands, “laying his right hand on the head of Ephraim, who was the younger, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.” David went out against the armed giant with nothing but faith: “You come to me with sword and spear and javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts.” So Christ defeated the enemy with the wood of the Cross.

The season of Sleebo turns our eyes to the end of time. Jesus speaks of signs in the sun, moon and stars, and of distress among nations; then “they will see ‘the Son of Man coming in a cloud’ with power and great glory.” In the evening Gospel “the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven”; many Fathers understood that sign to be the Cross. For believers this is not fear but hope: “stand up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”
conn: The bronze serpent.
Numbers 21:8–9 and John 3:14: look to the lifted-up Christ and live.
Crossed hands.
Genesis 48:14: Jacob's crossed hands, a figure of the Cross that blesses.
David and Goliath.
1 Samuel 17:45, 47: “the battle is the LORD's”; Christ conquers by the Cross.
The sign in heaven.
Matthew 24:30: the sign of the Son of Man, the Cross of glory.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is the sacrifice of the Cross made present. The priest blesses with the sign of the Cross; we sign ourselves with it; the Cross stands on the altar. The Thomas Christians of Kerala have always venerated the Cross without the corpus, the “Mar Thoma Sleeba”, as the sign of the risen Lord's victory.
outline: The bronze serpent and the crucified Christ.
Point 2 · He became a curse for us
“Stand up and raise your heads; your redemption is drawing near.”
live: Sign yourself with care
Make the sign of the Cross slowly and reverently each morning and night.
Venerate the Cross
Kiss or bow before the Cross at home or in church today.
Carry a cross with love
Offer a present suffering to God, united with Christ.
fathers: The sign of the Son of Man is the Cross, which will appear brighter than the sun, so that the Jews and all may see it and be without excuse (Homilies on Matthew 76).

Had there been no Cross, Christ would not have been crucified; had there been no Cross, life would not have been nailed to the tree. The Cross is called Christ's glory and his exaltation (Sermon 10 on the Exaltation of the Cross).
magis: Catechism 616–618
It is love to the end that confers on Christ's sacrifice its value of redemption; the Cross is the unique sacrifice of Christ.
Catechism 2157
The Christian begins his day, his prayers and his activities with the sign of the Cross.
Catechism 1186
The Cross and the altar are at the centre of the church building.
saints: 15 September: Our Lady of Sorrows. Sunday 19 September: I Sunday after Sleebo. Monday 20 September: Syro-Malankara Reunion Day (1930).
2027-09-14.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you were lifted up on the Cross to draw all people to yourself. Heal us of the poison of sin as we look to you; make us bless others with the sign of your Cross; and when your sign appears in heaven, let us raise our heads with joy, for our redemption is near. Amen.

2027-09-19.title: First Sunday after Sleebo
readings: The kingdom of God is among you; remember Lot's wife
Joseph's brothers come to Egypt for grain
They do not know the Lord
His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom
I dwell with the contrite and humble
Heaven must receive him until the time of universal restoration
The Spirit searches the depths of God
Keep awake, for you do not know when the time will come
2027-09-19.alt: Season of Sleebo. Monday 20 September: Syro-Malankara Reunion Day (1930), with its own readings.
2027-09-19.verse: Keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.
theo: The season of Sleebo teaches us to live awake. Jesus says: “From the fig tree learn its lesson: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts forth its leaves, you know that summer is near.” “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away. But about that day or hour no one knows… Beware, keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.” Christ will come again; we do not know when; therefore every day matters.

Jesus does not want fear but watchfulness. He gives the image of a man going on a journey who leaves his servants in charge, “each with his work”, and commands the doorkeeper to be on the watch. “Keep awake, for you do not know when the master of the house will come, in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or at dawn… And what I say to you I say to all: Keep awake.” To keep awake is to do faithfully the work he has given us.

In the evening Gospel the Pharisees ask when the kingdom will come. Jesus answers: “The kingdom of God is not coming with things that can be observed… the kingdom of God is among you.” It is already present in Christ. Yet he warns: as in the days of Noah, people ate and drank and married until the flood came. “Remember Lot's wife”, who looked back. “Those who try to make their life secure will lose it, but those who lose their life will keep it.”

St Peter tells the people that Jesus must remain in heaven “until the time of universal restoration that God announced long ago through his holy prophets.” St Paul says that the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God, and gives us to understand the gifts God has bestowed on us (1 Corinthians 2:10–12). Daniel proclaims: “his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom.” We wait, not anxiously, but with the Spirit's wisdom.
conn: Grain in Egypt.
Genesis 42: the brothers come hungry to Joseph, not knowing him; one day all will recognise Christ.
Not knowing the Lord.
Hosea 5:4: “they do not know the LORD”; watchfulness is knowing him now.
Everlasting kingdom.
Daniel 4:3: “his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom”; Mark 13:31: his words will not pass away.
Contrite hearts.
Isaiah 57:15: God dwells with the contrite and humble.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono we “proclaim the Lord's death until he comes” (1 Corinthians 11:26). Every Qurbono is an act of watchful waiting: Maranatha, Come, Lord.
outline: Point 1 · No one knows the hour
Christ will come; every day counts.
live: Daily examen
Each night ask: if the Lord came tonight, would he find me faithful?
Do your work well
Do your daily duties as service for the Lord.
Make peace now
Do not postpone reconciliation or confession.
fathers: He hid the hour from us so that we might be watchful, and each of us might think it could come in our own lifetime (Commentary on the Diatessaron 18, 15).

We preach not one coming of Christ only, but a second also, far more glorious than the first. The first was a sign of patience; the second brings the crown of the divine kingdom (Catechetical Lectures 15, 1).
magis: Catechism 673
Since the Ascension Christ's coming in glory has been imminent, even though we do not know the time.
Catechism 1036
The Lord's warnings about the last things are a call to responsibility and conversion: “watch!”
Catechism 2612
Vigilance is “custody of the heart”; Jesus asks for prayer that watches for his coming.
saints: Monday 20 September: Syro-Malankara Reunion Day. 21 September: St Matthew. 27 September: St Vincent de Paul. 29 September: Archangels Michael, Gabriel and Raphael.
2027-09-19.prayer: Lord Jesus, you will come again in glory, at an hour we do not know. Keep us awake and faithful, each in the work you have given us; let us not look back but forward; and fill us with your Spirit, so that when you come you may find us ready. Maranatha: come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

quick: Mary's birth is the dawn before the Sun of Justice, Christ.
She was full of grace from the first moment: “there is no flaw in you.”
Mary is great because she did the will of God.
2027-09-08.action: Honour Mary's birthday with a Rosary today.
2027-09-08.question: Am I being born anew each day into God's will?
2027-09-08.special: Nativity of Mary, Mother of God (Wednesday). End of the Eight Days' Fast.
illus: At Velankanni in Tamil Nadu, the feast of Our Lady's Nativity on 8 September draws pilgrims of every language and religion, many walking for days. A whole nation comes to wish a mother happy birthday.

family.explain: Today is Mother Mary's birthday! God made her full of grace so that she could be the mother of Jesus.
family.intention: We thank God for Mary and pray for all mothers and babies.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift can we give Mary on her birthday?”

catechism: Mary prepared for in the Old Testament.
kidsaint: The parents of Mary, the grandparents of Jesus. Tradition says they prayed for many years for a child, and God gave them Mary. Lesson: grandparents and parents who pray are a gift to the whole family.
term: The feast of Mary's birth on 8 September. The Church celebrates the birthdays of only three persons: Jesus (25 December), John the Baptist (24 June) and Mary (8 September).
termMore: The dogma defined by Pope Pius IX in 1854: from the first moment of her conception Mary was preserved, by a singular grace and in view of the merits of Christ, from every stain of original sin.

quick: The rich ruler lacked one thing: a free heart to follow Jesus.
“What is impossible for mortals is possible for God”: salvation is grace.
Pray always and do not lose heart; God will never forsake us.
2027-09-05.action: Ask in prayer: what still holds my heart back from following Jesus?
2027-09-05.question: What is the “one thing” I still lack?
2027-09-05.special: Fifth Sunday after the Transfiguration. Announce the Exaltation of the Holy Cross on Tuesday 14 September.
illus: A Kerala businessman made a fortune in the Gulf but felt empty. One day he began to give a tenth of his income to poor students. Years later he said: “I thought I was giving; I was really being set free.”

family.explain: A rich man wanted to follow Jesus but loved his money too much and went away sad. Jesus said: with God everything is possible!
family.intention: We pray for generous hearts that love Jesus more than things.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we love more than God? How can we share it?”

kidsaint: A rich young man who gave away everything, even his fine clothes, to follow Jesus and serve the poor. He became the happiest man in Italy. Lesson: the more we give, the freer and happier we become.
term: Jesus' image of something humanly impossible: a camel, the largest animal in Palestine, passing through the smallest opening. It shows that salvation depends on God's grace, not human power or wealth.
termMore: Poverty, chastity and obedience, which Jesus proposes to those who wish to follow him more closely (as to the rich young man). Religious men and women vow to live them; all Christians are called to their spirit.

quick: The Cross, sign of shame, has become the sign of victory and love.
Look to the lifted-up Christ, like the bronze serpent, and live.
The season of Sleebo looks to Christ's coming: “raise your heads.”
2027-09-14.action: Make the sign of the Cross slowly and reverently morning and night.
2027-09-14.question: Do I see my crosses in the light of Christ's Cross?
2027-09-14.special: Exaltation of the Holy Cross (Tuesday). The season of Sleebo begins.
illus: Ancient stone crosses, the “Persian crosses”, are kept in churches at Kottayam and Mylapore. They show a cross rising from a lotus, with a dove above: no body, only glory. Our ancestors saw the Cross as the tree of life.

family.explain: When snakes bit the people, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake; whoever looked at it was healed. Jesus on the Cross heals us when we look at him with faith.
family.intention: We pray to love the Cross of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Why do we make the sign of the Cross?”

kidsaint: The mother of Emperor Constantine. As an old woman she travelled to Jerusalem and, according to tradition, found the Cross of Jesus, and built churches at the holy places. Lesson: it is never too late to do something great for Jesus.
term: Syriac for “Cross”. The feast of the Holy Cross on 14 September begins the season of Sleebo, the last season of the Syro-Malankara year, which contemplates the Second Coming of Christ.
termMore: The cross of St Thomas: the ancient cross of the Thomas Christians, without a corpus, often rising from a lotus with a dove above, symbolising the risen Christ, the Holy Spirit and new life.

quick: “Keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.”
Watchfulness is faithfulness to the work the Lord has given us.
The kingdom is already among us; do not look back like Lot's wife.
2027-09-19.action: Each night this week ask: if the Lord came tonight, would he find me faithful?
2027-09-19.question: What would I change if I knew the Lord was coming this week?
2027-09-19.special: First Sunday after Sleebo. Monday 20 September: Reunion Day.
illus: A Kerala fisherman's wife keeps a lamp burning at the door when her husband is at sea, because she does not know what hour he will return. She does not sit idle; she works and waits. That is how the Church waits for Christ.

family.explain: Jesus will come again one day. We don't know when, so we should always be ready, doing good and loving God.
family.intention: We pray to be ready for Jesus every day.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be ready for Jesus today?”

kidsaint: A tax collector who sat at his booth counting money until Jesus said, “Follow me.” He got up at once and followed, and later wrote a Gospel. Lesson: when Jesus calls, be ready to say yes right away.
term: The last season of the Syro-Malankara liturgical year, from 14 September until the Sundays of the Consecration and Dedication of the Church, focusing on the Cross, the end of time and the Second Coming.
termMore: Aramaic: “Our Lord, come!” (1 Corinthians 16:22; Revelation 22:20), one of the oldest Christian prayers, expressing the Church's longing for Christ's return.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate a birthday: the birthday of our Mother. According to ancient tradition, a daughter was born to Joachim and Anna after many years of prayer, and they called her Mary. The world did not notice, but heaven rejoiced. St Andrew of Crete says: today the Creator of all has built himself a new temple.

In the garden after the first sin, God called: “Where are you?” Humanity was hiding in shame. But God did not abandon us. He promised a woman whose offspring would crush the serpent's head. Isaiah spoke of the virgin who would bear Immanuel. Mary's birth is the dawn; Christ is the sun that follows.

The Song of Songs says: “You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.” The Church sees Mary there: preserved by God's grace from all sin from the first moment of her life, so that she might be a pure dwelling for the Son of God. Her beauty is God's gift.

And yet Jesus says: “Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.” Mary is great not only because she was chosen, but because she said yes. On her birthday, let us give her the gift she loves most: a heart ready to do God's will. Let us also thank God for our own mothers, and pray for every child waiting to be born. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Mother Mary's birthday! Happy birthday, Mary!
God made Mary very special and full of grace, so she could be Jesus' mother.
What gift can you give Mary? A Hail Mary, and being kind like her!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a rich ruler came to Jesus and asked: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” He had kept the commandments since his youth. He was a good man. Jesus looked at him and said: “There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and give to the poor, and come, follow me.” And the man went away sad, because he was very rich.

Each of us has a “one thing”. It may be money, a career, a relationship, a habit, our reputation. Something we hold so tightly that we cannot follow Jesus with an open hand. Jesus is not against wealth as such; he is against wealth that owns us.

The disciples asked: “Then who can be saved?” And Jesus gave the answer that is our hope: “What is impossible for mortals is possible for God.” We cannot free ourselves; God can. And he promises that whoever leaves something for the kingdom will receive much more, in this life and eternal life to come. The Letter to the Hebrews says: “I will never leave you or forsake you.”

In the evening Gospel Jesus told us to pray always and not lose heart. Today, in prayer, ask the Lord: what is my one thing? And ask him to do the impossible: to set your heart free. On Tuesday we celebrate the Holy Cross, where Jesus gave everything for us. Let us learn from him to give. Amen.
kids: Children, a rich man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. Jesus said: share your things with the poor and follow me. But the man loved his money too much and went away sad.
Jesus said it is hard for rich people to enter heaven, as hard as a camel going through the hole of a needle!
But with God everything is possible! Let's ask Jesus to help us share our toys and things with others.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we lift up the Cross. For the Romans the cross was a sign of shame and the worst death. For us it is the sign of love and victory. According to tradition St Helena found the Cross in Jerusalem, and on this day it was raised before the people, who cried out: Lord have mercy.

In the desert, when serpents bit the people, God told Moses to set a bronze serpent on a pole; whoever looked at it lived. Jesus said: so must the Son of Man be lifted up. When we look at the crucified Christ with faith, we are healed of the poison of sin. St Paul says: Christ became a curse for us, to free us from the curse. He took our place.

The Fathers saw the Cross in many places of the Old Testament: in the crossed hands of Jacob blessing his grandsons, in the boy David going against Goliath with no sword but “in the name of the Lord.” The Cross looks weak, but it is God's power. Our ancestors in Kerala carved the Cross without the body, rising from a lotus, with the dove above: the Cross of glory.

Today begins the season of Sleebo, the last season of our year. Jesus speaks of signs in the sky and of his coming in glory. The Fathers say the sign of the Son of Man is the Cross. For those who love him, that day is not a terror: “stand up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.” Let us make the sign of the Cross with love today, and carry our crosses with him. Amen.
kids: Children, today we celebrate the Holy Cross! Jesus died on the Cross because he loves us so much.
Long ago, when snakes bit people, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake. Whoever looked at it was healed! Jesus on the Cross heals us too.
Let's make the sign of the Cross slowly: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus says: learn from the fig tree. When its branches become tender and leaves come out, you know summer is near. He speaks of his coming at the end of time, and says: “about that day or hour no one knows… Keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.”

Why did the Lord hide the hour? St Ephrem answers: he hid the hour so that we might be watchful, each thinking it could come in his own lifetime. If we knew the date, we would postpone conversion until the last minute. Because we do not know, every day is precious.

But watchfulness is not fear and not idleness. Jesus compares himself to a man who goes on a journey and gives each servant his work. To keep awake is to do our work faithfully: the mother caring for her family, the student studying honestly, the worker doing a full day's work, the priest serving his people. That is how we wait for the Lord.

In the evening Gospel Jesus says: “Remember Lot's wife”, who looked back and was lost. Do not look back with longing at sin. Look forward to Christ. Tomorrow we remember the Reunion of 1930, when our fathers did not look back but went forward into communion. This week, each night, ask: if the Lord came tonight, would he find me ready? Maranatha, come Lord Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus promised he will come back one day. When? Nobody knows, only God the Father!
So we must always be ready, like children waiting for their dad to come home, keeping the house clean and being good.
Every night, ask yourself: “Was I kind today? Did I pray?” That's how we are ready for Jesus!

intro: Today the Church rejoices at the birth of the Mother of God. According to ancient tradition she was born to Joachim and Anne. Her birth is the dawn that announces the rising of Christ, the Sun of justice. The Eight Days' Fast ends.

sub: The Song of Songs: “You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.”
The Church applies these words to Mary, preserved from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception (Pius IX, 1854).
The angel greets her as “favoured one”, full of grace.
q: You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.
And he came to her and said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.”
points.apply: Thank God for the gift of your own baptism, which washed away original sin.

sub: Isaiah promised a sign: a child named Immanuel.
Matthew sees the promise fulfilled in the virgin Mary and her Son.
Mary's birth prepares for the birth of “God with us”.
q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
All this took place to fulfill what had been spoken by the Lord through the prophet: “Look, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall name him Emmanuel,” which means, “God is with us.”
points.apply: Pray the Angelus at noon each day this week.

sub: Jesus says: whoever does the will of God is my mother.
Mary is blessed above all because she heard God's word and kept it.
She stood by the Cross: her whole life was a yes.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Make one decision this week by asking: what is God's will here?

concl: Mary's birth is a feast of hope: God's plan of salvation is moving toward its fulfilment.
Let us celebrate our Mother's birthday by becoming more like her.
2027-09-08.resolve: Celebrate the day as a family: honour mothers and grandmothers, and pray for them.

intro: Jesus urges us to pray always and not lose heart. A rich ruler goes away sad, unable to let go of his wealth, and Jesus says: what is impossible for mortals is possible for God. The Lord who comforts his people never forsakes us.

points.h: Pray always, do not lose heart
sub: Moses interceded for forty days for a sinful people.
The widow keeps knocking at the unjust judge's door; how much more will God hear his chosen ones.
Perseverance in prayer is faith that does not give up.
q: I prayed to the LORD and said, “Lord GOD, do not destroy the people who are your very own possession, whom you redeemed in your greatness, whom you brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.”
And will not God grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night? Will he delay long in helping them?
points.apply: Choose one intention you have stopped praying for, and take it up again daily.

sub: The rich ruler kept the commandments but could not let go of his wealth.
“How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
Salvation is not our achievement but God's gift; nothing is too wonderful for him.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD? At the set time I will return to you, in due season, and Sarah shall have a son.
He replied, “What is impossible for mortals is possible for God.”
points.apply: Name one attachment that holds you back from God, and loosen it by an act of generosity.

sub: “Comfort, O comfort my people”: God carries the lambs in his arms.
Be free from the love of money and content with what you have.
The Lord has said: “I will never leave you or forsake you.”
q: He will feed his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them in his bosom, and gently lead the mother sheep.
Keep your lives free from the love of money, and be content with what you have; for he has said, “I will never leave you or forsake you.”
points.apply: Thank God each night this week for three things you already have.

concl: Prayer that perseveres, hearts set free, and trust in the Shepherd: this is the way to the kingdom.
With God, all things are possible.
2027-09-05.resolve: Prepare for the feast of the Holy Cross on Tuesday with a good confession.

intro: Theme: “Lifted up, he draws all to himself.”
Today the Church lifts up the Holy Cross and the season of Sleebo, the last season of the liturgical year, begins. The instrument of death has become the tree of life and the sign of the Son of Man.

sub: In the desert, those bitten by serpents looked at the bronze serpent and lived.
Jesus applies this sign to himself: the Son of Man must be lifted up.
We look to the Cross in faith and receive eternal life.
q: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.” So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
points.apply: Spend five minutes this week simply looking at a crucifix in silent prayer.

points.h: He became a curse for us
sub: Jacob crossed his hands to bless: the Fathers saw here a figure of the Cross.
Christ took our curse upon himself so that the blessing of Abraham might reach all nations.
The Cross is not defeat but the place where love wins.
q: But Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it on the head of Ephraim, who was the younger, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.”
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross slowly and reverently each morning and evening.

sub: David faced Goliath not with armour but in the name of the Lord.
At the end the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven.
Christians do not fear the end; they lift their heads, for redemption is near.
q: But David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with sword and spear and javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.”
Now when these things begin to take place, stand up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.
points.apply: Face one fear this week in the name of the Lord, holding the cross.

concl: The Cross is our hope, our weapon and our glory.
We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world.
2027-09-14.resolve: Venerate the Cross at home as a family and bless your children with the sign of the cross.

intro: In the season of Sleebo the Church looks toward the end of history and the coming of the Lord. Jesus says the kingdom is already among us, warns us not to look back like Lot's wife, and tells us to stay awake. Tomorrow we celebrate Reunion Day.

sub: The kingdom does not come with signs that can be observed; it is already present in Jesus.
Nebuchadnezzar confessed: God's kingdom is everlasting.
We meet the kingdom in the word, the sacraments and the poor.
q: How great are his signs, how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his sovereignty is from generation to generation.
The kingdom of God is not coming with things that can be observed; nor will they say, ‘Look, here it is!’ or ‘There it is!’ For, in fact, the kingdom of God is among you.
points.apply: Look for one sign of God's kingdom in your daily life and give thanks for it.

sub: Lot's wife looked back toward Sodom and was lost.
Clinging to the old life prevents us from following Christ.
Those who lose their life for him will keep it.
q: But Lot's wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
Remember Lot's wife. Those who try to make their life secure will lose it, but those who lose their life will keep it.
points.apply: Let go of one past grievance or habit that keeps you looking back.

sub: The Holy One dwells with the contrite and humble.
No one knows the day or hour; so we watch.
Watchfulness means daily faithfulness, not fear.
q: For thus says the high and lofty one who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with those who are contrite and humble in spirit.
Beware, keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.
points.apply: End each day with a short examination of conscience.

concl: The kingdom is near, the past is behind, the Lord is coming.
Let us keep awake and pray for the unity of the Church as we celebrate Reunion Day.
2027-09-19.resolve: Pray tomorrow for the unity of all the St Thomas Christians.
